From the front desk personnel to the intern to the tech to the vet, my dog and I felt cared for and heard. The tech and vet were supportive and understanding that I could not afford the more traditional path of treating my dog. They listened carefully to what I had been doing and were affirming, encouraging and added a few ideas. They also laid out a plan I could afford if I chose to go a different route. The tech, Michael, was full of encouragement and understanding, and he even carried my dog out to my car after, since it's hard for my dog to jump in and he is very heavy for me to lift. The clinic is clean and organized, the prices up front and affordable. I was so impressed, and these are our people now. The expensive suburban vet is out. A special shout-out to the intern, who was there mostly to observe. She sat on the floor in the corner and my dog immediately went to her and sat on her lap. He does that with people he loves and trusts. And at one point she spoke up and said some very true and truly kind, but not often voiced, observations about me and Buddy. I hope she decides to pursue vet medicine. I think she will be great whatever direction her life takes her. Thank you! One note: you won't be able to reach them on the phone they are so busy, so go ahead and make an appointment request online or just go by in person to schedule. I understand they also take walk-ins but waits can be long. With an appointment, there was no wait.

Nicer facility and you get to be in with your pet now. I like that. But $165 for shots for 1 dog, and 4 months of heart worm treatment is still really expensive.  They make owning a dog for just the RICH. Which means more dogs and cats euthanized. We need more affordable prices. 😡 …

I brought my dog in for her first year immunizations and an ear issue. I expressed to the doctor that her ear was really bothering her, that I didn’t feel like it was just excess ear wax. He insisted it was just dirty ears, told us there was no need to test her for an ear injection and sold us a $30 bottle of ear cleaner. A week later I took her to another vet and they diagnosed her with a severe double lateral fungal ear infection. So extra cost of a second vet visit and unnecessary discomfort for my dog. Needless to say, I won’t be bringing any of my dogs here.

I went to get my 4 month old German shepard I had recently gotten to get his 4 months vaccines. When we came it everything was alright, the service was great, cheap price and we didn't wait long. Afterwards it was our turn and we took our puppy in, the doctor (I assume is the main doctor since he was walking in and out for each dog) weighed him and everything was going  great, But as soon as we enter for his check-up our puppy didn't look really well and they started with his check-up and then we had put our puppy down and thats when everything started.

Rey (our puppy) started having a bloddy diahearra on the floor and the "Doctor" was being so un-proffesional and screaming, "OH NO, NO, NO ,NO" and we were confused, obviously we were shocked he did that because it was his first time doing that, then the 'Doctor' ran out of the room and told his assistant to get out too. Then he came back and said "I will be right back with napkins so you can clean up".......I'M SORRY??? He wanted us to clean up the bloody diahearra from the floor and procceeds to give us 3 napkins without explaining what was wrong with our dog. Absolutely unacceptable. About 5 minutes later, the janitor comes to clean up the mess and she was very polite, but we were still confused what was going on and what Rey had. She then explained to us that had 'Parvo-virus' with has NO cure and is contagious with other young dogs, and after everything was cleaned up, the 'Doctor' came and just stood there with his hands on his hips looking at Rey and repeatedly kept saying "Oh no, this is not good, no, no ,this is very bad, *deep sigh*, no, no ,no", we asked him concerned what was wrong with our dog and he just said, 'he has parvo-virus' and then explains what it does, and how there is no cure and how even if he were to get treatment is would be a 50/50 chance he lived and we had researched that puppies living with this virus have a 91% chance of NOT making it, so it would've been useless to make our poor puppy to suffer and not be able to make it in the end. I then ask him how long it would be if we kept him in his final days like this and he was short with his response and didn't let me finish, I had said, "If we were to keep him with us like this in his final days woul---" "I don't know."     Just like that.  He then continued with his nonsense of "Oh no, not good" instead of keeping his mouth shut. another man came in only to briefly spray some disinfectant spray  in the door, while we were tearing up at the fact that our dog will not make it, and this dumb unproffesional doctor starts LAUGHING??? Beacuse this man sprayed in the room???? How is this funny?? My mom and I look at him angry and another assistant that was there told him to please step out of the room. the assistants more proffessional and great at explaining than the doctor. We were then just in the room crying because Rey wouldn't make it and this man couldn't "Read the Room" as our dog was laying weakly on the foor and he just stayed in the doorway looking at our dog just sighing and in the end since this was contagious and the probabilaty of him living is near 0% and price for the treatment was from $800-$1,000's of dollars which we do NOT have, we had no choice but to sleep our baby :(

overall, this was one of the worst experiances I have ever had in my life, no respect for us or our dog.

Adopted a cat from the shelter that was to young to get vaccinated. So I was told to come back in two weeks. He had ringworms and it took a long time to get rid of. It infected my other cat I already had as well. I didn't want to bring him in and infect other animals. When it finally went away about 4 months passed and they told me I had to pay for the fees and both the shots he was supposed to get. Even tho I was told by the shelter I could just walk in and get them free. Because why else did I pay $100 adoption fee. When the site states vaccines are included. They also questioned why I waited 7 months. I didn't realize at the time they looked at his birthday and not when I adopted him.  I agreed because I live an hour away and don't want to wait to long to bring him back home. I also have autism so I know Im not the best at interactions like this.  At the end they told me they took the fee off and the rabbies off and I only had to pay $21. At the time they went through some type of system change so I was being understanding and patient. My bank showed that it charged me full price and when I brought it up I was told she only charged me for the $21. No other acknowledgement or to double check if there was a mistake made. I was like...OK. maybe it's just a pending hold? When it stopped pending in my bank account and still stated the full amount was charged I called back and I was told the manager wasn't there that day and that I would get a call back soon. I didn't. I called back again and they told me something about the company working on it and I should get it soon and they would call me back. I haven't. Both times I've been forgotten and I don't really want to call back another time. I haven't been rude and I've been patient the whole time and just followed instructions from the shelter when I adopted my kitty. I even sent an email that's been ignored.  If I would have known I would spend that much I would have gone to something local and saved my money. I feel very disrespected and dismissed on my time, money, and efforts. I paid $72 for something thay was supposed to be included with the adoption. And I know there's a fee to pay but I asked the day I adopted my cat if I had to pay extra when I brought him back for his vaccines and they told me no. So that was my expectation going in.
